in_arabic.name: أَسْكَرِيَّةٌ
in_arabic.meaning: أَسْكَرِيَّةٌ الاسم هو مصدر مصدر، يعني «الذات المسلحة»
in_arabic.long_meaning: أَسْكَرِيَّةٌ الاسم هو مصدر مصدر، يعني «الذات المسلحة» وهو مصدر من «أَسْكَرَ» وهو مصدر من «سَكَرَ» يعني «مسلح» والذات تشير إلى الجسم الإنساني، وتحمل المعنى الرئيسي للذات المسلحة، وتشير إلى الجسم الإنساني الذي يرتبط بالسلاح، وتشير أيضًا إلى الجسم الذي يتميز بالعزيمة والشجاعة، وتحمل أيضًا المعنى المتأخر للجسم الذي يكون مصدرًا للقوة والسلطة، وتشير أيضًا إلى الجسم الإنساني الذي يتميز بالسلاح والقوة، وعادةً ما يتم استخدام هذا الاسم للإشارة إلى الصبية والفتيات الذين يتميزون بالشجاعة والقوة

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic history, Askariyah refers to the military forces that protected the Islamic lands and the most sacred Islamic sites, such as the Prophet Muhammad's mosque in Medina. The Askariyah played a crucial role in defending the early Muslim community from external threats, particularly during the Ridda Wars and the Battle of Tabuk. Their courage, discipline, and devotion to their faith made them an essential part of Islamic culture and served as a model of dedication and self-sacrifice for future generations.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Askariyah holds deep spiritual significance as it represents one's role as a protector and defender of faith and community. In Islamic teachings, every believer is considered a soldier in the path of God, responsible for preserving their faith, their families, and their communities. The name Askariyah serves as a reminder of the importance of being vigilant in safeguarding our spiritual and moral selves, as well as the world around us. It also symbolizes the idea that every individual has a responsibility to protect and serve others, fostering sentiments of compassion, love, and unity within the Islamic community.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: The Askariyah are a Shia Islamic sect named after the eponymous city of Askara (modern day Samarra) in present-day Iraq. Askariyah emerged as a distinct Shia group in the 9th century CE during the Abbasid Caliphate.
historical_references.context: Emergence of the Askariyah Shia sect in the Abbasid Caliphate, Iraq

historical_references.reference: The Askariyah believe that the Twelfth Imam of Shia Islam, also known as the Imam Mahdi, went into hiding in Samarra around 874 CE and will reappear at the end of time.
historical_references.context: Belief in the occultation of the Twelfth Imam and his alleged hiding in Samarra, leading to the naming of the Askariyah sect.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Askariyah remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.

name_in_real_life.story: Aisha Askariyah from Istanbul, Turkey embodies the meaning of Askariyah - "Soldier, protector". Growing up, they were known for their strong character and deep faith, always striving to live up to the beautiful significance of their name.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Askariyah signifies the protective and guardian role of the believer in upholding and preserving the faith. It is a reminder of the spiritual duty to safeguard the teachings of Islam and shield it from harm. As followers of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), we are all Askariyah, committed to defending and spreading the message of peace, unity, and submission to Allah.
